subject: Spend safety net / behaviour when hosted API usage exceeds budget
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy@fuelmetrics.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit@fuelmetrics.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: what happens if we exceed our monthly budget?

Hi Rishi,

Quick question as we finalize our internal procurement — if FuelMetrics exceeds the committed monthly budget for the hosted API, what will actually happen from a runtime and billing perspective? A few sub-questions:

- Will calls be blocked automatically when a spend cap is hit, or will we continue to be billed for overage?
- Are there intermediate throttles / rate reductions vs a hard stop?
- How are in-flight requests handled when a cap is reached (do they complete or get cut off)?
- If we accidentally spike one day, is there an automatic refund/credit or is that handled case-by-case?

We’re trying to map this to our monthly billing guardrails — any short bullets and an example (e.g., committed $10k/month -> what happens at $10,100) would help.

Thanks — Lucy
Lucy Chen
Head of ML, FuelMetrics
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@fuelmetrics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: what happens if we exceed our monthly budget?

Hi Lucy — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: we support multiple behaviours and can configure whichever matches FuelMetrics’ billing guardrails. Longer answer below with an example. Attaching the current rate card for reference (Redwood_rate_card_v3.pdf).

Options we offer (configurable per account or per API key):

1) Hard spend cap (stop):
- Behaviour: Once the account hits the configured dollar cap for the billing period, new requests receive 429 ("quota exceeded"). In-flight requests are allowed to complete; we do not truncate responses mid-stream.
- Billing: No additional charges beyond the cap for that billing period.

2) Soft cap + throttle + alerts (preferred for availability):
- Behaviour: At threshold (e.g., 95% of cap) we send notifications and progressively throttle new requests (configurable steps: 75% -> 50% -> 25% throughput). Throttling is implemented at the routing layer; some requests may queue briefly depending on burst settings.
- Billing: Any consumption still counts toward usage and is billed. Throttling reduces burn rate but does not guarantee zero overage.

3) Auto-top-up (preapproved payment):
- Behaviour: If enabled, hitting the cap triggers an automatic increment (you set an increment amount or percent). Calls continue without interruption.
- Billing: Charged against the card on file or net of pre-funded balance.

4) Overage billing (pay-as-you-go after cap):
- Behaviour: We keep serving; overage is billed at the published overage rate (example below).
- Billing: Overages show as a separate line item on the invoice.

Example (committed $10,000/month):
- Hard cap: traffic stops at $10,000; you will see 429s if you attempt to exceed.
- Soft cap: at $9,500 we notify and throttle; if you continue, you may be billed for $10,100.
- Auto-top-up: you can set a $1,000 buffer, so service continues and you are charged $11,000 total.
- Overage billing: overage billed at committed rate or negotiated add-on (e.g., committed price + 25% for uncommitted usage).

Operational notes:
- We can implement a short grace window (e.g., 60 seconds) to allow spiky bursts to finish; default is to allow previously accepted requests to complete.
- Refunds and credits for accidental overage are handled by Support / Finance and evaluated case-by-case; for new enterprise customers we sometimes offer a one-time courtesy credit (not guaranteed).

If you want, Marissa can share a draft SLA that spells out the exact language for Hard Cap vs Overage behaviour.

Next steps: I can (a) toggle a Hard Cap for your test API key, (b) enable soft-cap throttling with 95% notify, or (c) set up auto-top-up. Which would you like us to enable for the pilot?

— Rishi

Thanks Rishi — super helpful. Couple quick clarifications: 

- In-flight requests allowed to complete is good to know. What happens if a long-running streaming generation is in progress when the cap is hit — is that guaranteed to finish or do you have SLOs that allow cutting streams?
- For soft-cap throttling, is throttling deterministic (e.g., every Nth request) or probabilistic (sampled)? We need something that won’t bias certain users or endpoints.
- We need clarity on refunds: our procurement team wants to know under what circumstances Redwood would issue credits automatically 

Also — is there a way to model a "safety buffer" for the first month (e.g., 10% free buffer) so we won’t be penalized for onboarding spikes? It would make internal approval much easier.

Happy to hop on a quick call if that’s easier.

— Lucy

On Mon, Mar 16, 2026 at 08:45 AM Lucy Chen <lucy@fuelmetrics.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rishi — super helpful. Couple quick clarifications:
>
> - In-flight requests allowed to complete is good to know. What happens if a long-running streaming generation is in progress when the cap is hit — is that guaranteed to finish or do you have SLOs that allow cutting streams?
> - For soft-cap throttling, is throttling deterministic (e.g., every Nth request) or probabilistic (sampled)? We need something that won’t bias certain users or endpoints.
> - We need clarity on refunds: our procurement team wants to know under what circumstances Redwood would issue credits automatically

Hi Lucy — answering inline: 

- Streaming / in-flight: we let accepted connections finish streaming; the runtime will not force-close a connection mid-stream in normal operation. If the account is placed into a hard stop via manual admin action, we will still let currently accepted requests finish. There are rare operational events (zone failovers) where streams may be cut, but those are covered under the SLA and compensated separately.

- Throttling algorithm: currently we support both deterministic quota-based throttles and probabilistic shedding. For soft-cap we typically recommend deterministic rate-limits per API key (tokens per second ceiling) to avoid sampling bias across endpoints. If you prefer fair probabilistic sampling across endpoints, we can enable that for specific keys.

- Refunds / credits: automatic refunds are not standard. However, for onboarding customers we can agree to a one-time safety buffer (e.g., 10% of committed monthly spend) as a free credit that is applied automatically in the first billing cycle. Beyond that, credits are issued after a support ticket review and Finance approval (case-by-case). We can bake the one-time buffer into the initial commercial terms.

I attached a short draft SLA that includes the exact wording for Hard Cap behaviour and streaming guarantees (Redwood_draft_sla_fuelmetrics.docx).

Operational suggestion: we can enable the following for your pilot:
- 10% onboarding buffer applied automatically in month 1
- Soft-cap at 95% with deterministic throttling at 50% throughput step, and alerts to your billing contacts
- Option to enable auto-top-up for production after pilot (pre-authorized card or invoiced top-ups)

If that sounds good I can send a short amendment to the quote and Ben can confirm the overage pricing.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
